title: Embeddings & Reranking Discovery - Redwood <> NebulaAI
summary: Initial discovery covering NebulaAI's current vector search stack, integration needs for embeddings and reranking, throughput/dimensionality targets, hybrid search use cases, and security constraints. Agreed next steps: run hosted benchmark, share security pack, and scope dedicated/private options if throughput or data residency requires it.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-12 11:00am PT / 15:00Z - 45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Dr. Arjun Rao (CTO, NebulaAI), Sofia Martinez (Head of Search), Ben Cho (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros then we can jump in. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, Liam's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Arjun: Hi all, Arjun here. Thanks for doing this. We wanted to walk through how you'd handle embeddings + rerank at scale, and clarify hosted vs dedicated for us.
[00:22] Sofia: Yeah mainly focused on search relevance and perf. We currently run an Elastic cluster fronted by a vector layer.
[00:30] Liam: got it, thanks. Could you give a quick overview of current stack and numbers?
[00:36] Ben: Sure - we index ~40M docs, average doc embedding dim is 1536 (we use text-embedding-3-ish models), we serve ~1.2k qps peak, sustained ~300 qps. Latency SLO for first-stage is 100-200ms and rerank ideally sub-300ms additional.
[00:55] Maya: ok that's helpful, so first-stage ANN + then a reranker model in ranker stage?
[01:01] Sofia: Exactly. We do BM25 to shortlist 100 -> dense ANN to 10 -> rerank via a cross-encoder. We're evaluating moving embeddings off our infra.
[01:12] Liam: For that flow Redwood supports either hosted embedding generation or you can bring your own and use Redwood's reranking/serving. For vector DB we integrate with Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, plus you can push results to Elastic/OpenSearch for hybrid.
[01:28] Arjun: We want to keep our vector DB on-prem for compliance but maybe run reranker in hosted; is that common?
[01:34] Liam: Yep, hybrid is common. Many customers run their vector DB in their VPC or on-prem and call Redwood via private deploy or via secure peering; alternatively you can call hosted Redwood to generate embeddings and push vectors to the customer DB. There are tradeoffs re: egress and latency.
[01:48] Ben: For peering, do you support VPC peering or private link? We need to avoid public egress.
[01:53] Maya: We support VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated/Private; hosted has secure TLS endpoints but for no-egress you'd look at Private deployment. We'll share network docs.
[02:03] Sofia: One big question is dimensionality. We've seen 1536 vs 1024 sizing effects. What's your guidance?
[02:09] Liam: It depends on model and recall requirements. For semantic search 1536 embeddings (e.g., model variants) give slightly better recall on our evals, but cost and vector DB index size grows linearly. For many customers 1024 is a good compromise. We can run Nebula's sample queries against both and show tradeoffs.
[02:25] Arjun: And for throughput, if we host reranker on Redwood hosted what's the p95 token latency?
[02:31] Liam: For a cross-encoder rerank on a 1k token context, on Hosted using optimized models we typically see p50 ~60-120ms and p95 ~220-400ms depending on model and batch. Dedicated gives lower variance and higher throughput. There's also batching and KV cache considerations.
[02:47] Ben: How does batching affect latency for requests that need near-real-time? We can't batch too long.
[02:52] Liam: You can configure batching windows; Redwood's runtime supports micro-batching down to a few ms but there's always tradeoff between per-token cost and latency. For sub-100ms SLOs you'd probably want Dedicated with predictable throughput and reserved capacity.
[03:06] Sofia: We're also exploring reranking as a fusion model: combining BM25 score + embedding similarity + learned reranker score. Any built-in support?
[03:14] Maya: We have first-class support for hybrid pipelines. You can send BM25 scores as metadata, do vector similarity in the vector DB, and then run a reranker. Our SDKs include examples for score fusion and reweighting.
[03:23] Arjun: Storage: snapshotting embeddings, can Redwood store embeddings for us or do you recommend customer DB?
[03:29] Liam: Both options. Hosted Redwood can persist vectors for you (storage add-on) but for strict residency customers usually keep vectors in their DB and only call Redwood for generation/serving. For private deployments you can fully control vector persistence.
[03:41] Ben: Any notes on index type? HNSW vs IVF?
[03:44] Liam: HNSW is default for recall/latency tradeoffs. For very large corpora IVF+PQ can be useful to reduce memory. We can advise based on your data shape after review of a sample.
[03:55] Sofia: Security - we need SOC2 Type II, SSO (SAML), customer-managed KMS, audit logs.
[04:02] Maya: Redwood is SOC2, support SSO/SAML, RBAC in the Console, and we offer KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private. We'll share the security pack and network diagram after the call.
[04:12] Arjun: Great. Also curious about cost: embeddings generation vs storing vs reranking per 1k qps.
[04:19] Liam: We typically break cost into three: embedding generation (per embedding), vector storage/ops (index costs on DB), and rerank compute (per query tokens). Hosted usage pricing is per-token + per-embedding; Dedicated is commit-based and gives better unit economics at high QPS. We can run a cost projection after we see your sample workload.
[04:36] Ben: We have GDPR/data residency constraints in EU for some datasets — would Private deployment be required?
[04:42] Maya: If you need full control and isolation, Private or Dedicated in your region is recommended. Private gives customer-managed control plane and on-prem option. We'll map options to your compliance needs.
[04:53] Sofia: Any known misc issues integrating with Weaviate? We use it for semantic metadata.
[04:58] Liam: Weaviate integrates well; note the hybrid search semantics can differ across DBs — we'll help tune the scoring function. Also watch out for metadata cardinality that can impact index performance.
[05:10] Arjun: Can you demo a quick benchmark?
[05:12] Liam: We can run a hosted benchmark quickly: you provide a 1% sample of docs and query traces, we'll run both 1024 and 1536 embed configs and a rerank pass, return p50/p95 latencies and recall metrics. It usually takes 3-5 business days to run and analyze.
[05:26] Maya: next steps - we'll send a benchmark ask, security docs, and a pricing sketch. Also schedule follow-up with infra to scope Dedicated if numbers indicate.
[05:35] Ben: Sounds good. Any competitors you think we should be cautious of?
[05:38] Maya: Pinecone is common for hosted vectors; Elastic/OpenSearch folks will argue for integrated approach. Weaviate is common with hybrid metadata-first use cases. We'll include notes comparing them.
[05:50] Arjun: ok thanks, we'll get you the sample and I expect we'll try the hosted benchmark first.
[05:55] Maya: Great thanks everyone.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts ("KV cash" for KV cache, "V-P-C" spoken) and some proper nouns slightly off. Shared artifacts referenced: security pack (link sent after call), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), pricing sketch (to be shared).

Liam - Share benchmark sheet + initial throughput expectations (p50/p95) by 2027-05-16
Arjun - Provide sample dataset snapshot and query patterns by 2027-05-18
